title: Wiener Schnitzel
subtitle: Breaded pork escalope, golden and crispy
excerpt: Pork loin is hammered thin, coated in flour, egg, and panko breadcrumbs, then fried in butter and oil until golden. The crust should be light and crispy, not thick or stodgy. Serve with a wedge of lemon.
sourceNotes: Based on the Austrian original. Pork loin escalopes are a standard substitute for veal in home cooking.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Bread the escalopes up to 2 hours ahead. Keep uncovered in the fridge so the coating dries out a little before frying.

content.text: The escalopes need to be very thin, about 4mm. Thicker pork will not cook through before the crust burns. Use a rolling pin or the flat side of a heavy pan to beat them out.
Set up three flat plates in a row: flour, beaten egg, and panko breadcrumbs.
Season the escalopes with salt on both sides.
Dust each escalope in flour. Shake off the excess. Dip in egg. Let the excess drip off. Press gently into the breadcrumbs on both sides.
Heat the butter and oil together in a large frying pan over medium-high heat.
When the butter foams, add two escalopes. Cook for 3 minutes each side until deep golden. Do not press them down.
Drain on kitchen paper. Cook the remaining two escalopes. Add a little more butter if the pan looks dry.
Serve at once with lemon wedges.

items.cause: Too much flour or egg not dried before crumbing
items.fix: Shake off excess flour and let egg drip off first.

items.symptom: Breadcrumbs are burning before pork is cooked
items.fix: Reduce to medium heat and cook 1 minute longer.

items.cause: Pan not hot enough or too much butter pooled
items.fix: Drain on a rack, not paper, to keep the crust crisp.
